content: Amlexanox is a medication specifically prescribed for the treatment of aphthous ulcers, commonly known as canker sores. It works by reducing the time it takes for these ulcers to heal, which in turn alleviates the associated pain. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor, dentist, or pharmacist for further details. Amlexanox is available as a beige-colored paste. It should be applied as soon as symptoms of an ulcer are noticed. Typically, it is used four times daily—after brushing and flossing your teeth following breakfast, lunch, dinner, and before bedtime. After application, wash your hands immediately. This medication should only be used until the ulcer has healed, which usually occurs within 10 days. If significant healing has not occurred within this timeframe, contact your physician or dentist. Always follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your healthcare provider if you have any questions. Use amlexanox exactly as directed, and do not use more or less of it or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Before using amlexanox, inform your doctor, dentist, or pharmacist if you are allergic to amlexanox or any other medications. Additionally, disclose all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including vitamins and herbal supplements. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your healthcare provider. Should you become pregnant while using amlexanox, contact your doctor or dentist immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Amlexanox may cause minor side effects, such as mild pain, stinging, or burning sensations on the skin that come and go, as well as nausea or diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor or dentist. In rare cases, amlexanox may cause a rash. If this occurs, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program, either online or by phone. Store amlexanox in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Amlexanox is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, and if accidental contact occurs, rinse your eyes thoroughly. Do not share this medication with others. Keep all appointments with your doctor or dentist, and inform them if your ulcers worsen or fail to improve within 10 days. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. The brand name for amlexanox is Aphthasol®.
